abstract: We proposed a power efficient Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (QAM) modulation scheme for Rayleigh fading channel, which varies the number of modulation levels in accordance with the wireless fading channel variation. We first review the various kinds of adaptive modulation techniques, concerning their goals, methods and results. Then we proposed our system architecture and framing arrangement, using a unmodulated pulse to indicate the channel fading state, and 3 identical modulation identifiers to determine which modulation constellation is used in the remaining QAM symbols. After that we derived our MQAM signal constellation, and compare it with star-constellation MQAM. The result shows that it can greatly decrease the power consumption, and will achieve better Peak Power-Average Power performance. We present closed-form of adaptation boundaries for these constellations, computer simulation is also made to demonstrate our scheme optimizes transmission.

articleTitle: The modified Hamming bound for unequal error protection codes
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: The modified Hamming bound for unequal error protection (UEP) codes is derived. Based on the code symbol separation vector of UEP codes, we derived the large weight error pattern correction criterion for a given UEP code. The criterion is also valid for non-linear UEP codes. Furthermore, the modified Hamming bound for UEP codes can also be applied to non-linear UEP codes.

articleTitle: On absolute stability of delayed neural networks
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: This paper first investigates the absolute exponential stability (AEST) of delayed neural networks with a general class of partially Lipschitz continuous and monotone increasing activation functions. The main results obtained are that if the interconnection matrix T of the delayed neural networks satisfies that -T is an H -matrix with nonnegative diagonal elements and there exists k satisfying the condition concerned, then the neural network system is absolutely stable (ABST).

articleTitle: Can tree adjunct grammar guided genetic programming be good at finding a needle in a haystack? A case study
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: In this paper, we experiment with tree-adjunct grammar guided genetic programming (TAG3P) on even parity problems in order to investigate the robustness of TAG3P on the problems classified as "finding a needle in a haystack". We compare the result with grammar guided genetic programming (GGGP) and genetic programming (GP). The results show that TAG3P does not work well on the problems due to the nature of the search space and the structure of the solution.

articleTitle: Practical power loss analysis simulator of soft switching and hard switching PWM inverters and performance evaluations
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: This paper deals with a feasible power loss analysis simulator which can actually estimate the total power losses of three phase voltage source soft-switching inverter as well as hard-switching inverter. To estimate switching power losses and conduction power losses of switching semiconductor power devices - IGBTs, incorporated into the inverters and converters - this practical simulator is based on making use of feasible switching power loss data-based table and conduction power loss table which are accumulated from the measured transient switching operation and periodic steady-state conduction voltage and current operating waveforms of semiconductor switching power devices used in the power converters. The effectiveness of feasible simulation technique and power loss evaluations for power electronic conversion circuits and systems has been confirmed on the basis of simulation and experimental results under the conditions of soft switching and hard switching PWM schemes.

articleTitle: A 6-bit 150 MHz competition encoding flash analog-to-digital converter
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: A CMOS 6 bit 150 MHz flash analog-to-digital converter, fully compatible with standard digital CMOS technology, is described. Compared with the conventional encoding structure, competition encoding can reduce the comparator's power consumption as well as suppress the error code rate of the ADC output greatly. The chip, fabricated in standard 0.35 /spl mu/m 3.3 V CMOS technology, occupies an area of 0.64/spl times/0.45 mm/sup 2/. Finally, some test results are presented.

articleTitle: Optimal transform for colored noise suppression
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: There has been interest in the application of filter banks and transforms to noise suppression. Recently, Akkarakaran and Vaidyanathan (2001) showed that when the noise is white, the optimal transform (not necessary unitary) for noise suppression is the Karhunen-Loeve transform (KLT). Moreover they showed that for the case of colored noise, if both the noise and signal have a common KLT, then the KLT is optimal for subband noise suppression. In this paper, we derive the optimal transform (not restricting to the class of unitary transforms) for the noise suppression problem when the signal and noise have arbitrary spectrum.

articleTitle: Research on bandwidth management mechanism of resilient packet ring
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: Resilient packet ring (RPR) is the main trend for metropolitan area networks (MAN). At present, it is still in the early research and development stage. Bandwidth (BW) management is an important subject of media access control (MAC) in RPR networks. Based on studying a series of proposed standard drafts of BW management, we present a new BW management mechanism of RPR. By using BW allocation and access rate control, the new mechanism can achieve maximum BW capacity of the ring and avoid head-of-line (HOL) blocking of the network.

articleTitle: Design of carrier recovery for QAM/VSB dual mode
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: In this paper, an architecture and hardware implementation of the carrier recovery (CR) used in dual mode (QAM and VSB) transceiver for digital CATV is proposed. The proposed CR uses decision-directed approach with steep gradient algorithm, which can be used in both QAM and VSB signal. Thus, the hardware complexity for dual mode is dramatically reduced, while the performance is almost the same. To increase the acquisition range of CR, a frequency locked loop (FLL) is used in VSB mode while a derotator/rotator pair is adopted in QAM mode. As a result, the CR can reach /spl plusmn/100 KHz acquisition range. Finally, the CR is implemented by TSMC 0.35um 1P4M process. The total gate is 20820 and the maximum symbol rate is 21.52 M Baud.

articleTitle: Visual fuzzy recognition of the object nameplate in video sequences
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: This paper presents an approach of the fuzzy recognition of the object nameplate in video sequences based on computer vision. After the nameplate character image is layered, the critical points and critical line part can be extracted in the layers of the images. According to the stroke extracting regularity, the critical points and line parts can be merged into strokes. The stroke structure is used to describe the spatial relation of the conjoint strokes. The text image can be mapped into the feature space of the stroke and stroke structure. In the visual feature space, a fuzzy classifier is extensively used. The visual fuzzy recognition can much improve the recognition of the rotated, distorted, deformed and defiled text image in the video sequences. Experiments carried out on large data sets of video sequences, automatically recognized the licenses of the automobiles in real time, show very promising results.

articleTitle: A scalable pattern recognition method
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: This paper put forward a scalable pattern recognition system that has a knowledge-increasable ability for solving problems of complex or large quantities of classes. Since multiple classifiers work in parallel during the training process and dynamic grouping technique is adopted on recognition, performance on both scalability and recognition rate has improved greatly. Our method can not only accelerate calculation speed and improve recognition rate but also be extended easily and freely. It can be used in pattern recognition such as face, fingerprint and character. The constructive method of the system shows the generality. Experimental results prove its reasonableness and feasibility.

articleTitle: A new family of carrier lock detectors and E/sub s//N/sub 0/ estimators for M-PSK receivers
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: A family of carrier lock detectors for M-PSK receivers operating in AWGN channels is suggested. The statistical properties of the lock detectors are derived theoretically using stochastic analysis, and computer simulations are used to validate the results obtained. The derivations yield discovery of two useful attributes of the lock detectors: (1) They are self-normalizing (or in other words signal-level independent), and (2) The channel E/sub s//N/sub 0/ can be readily ascertained from their value when the receiver is in lock. Furthermore, a particularly simple hardware implementation for the lock metric computation process is found, which allows easy and efficient implementation of its computation within an FPGA or ASIC.

articleTitle: A delay sub-space decomposition algorithm of electroencephalography sources localization
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: We present a new EEG inverse algorithm utilized for extracting multi-sources in EEGs. It is based on multiple signal classification (MUSIC). A delay-correlation matrix instead of the previous zero-delay-correlation matrix is introduced to conduct the signal-sub-space estimate in the MUSIC algorithm to get a better performance when coping with spatially coherent noise disturbances. The effectiveness of the delay MUSIC (DM) is confirmed by the final promising results of a simulation test.

articleTitle: Modeling of supercritical fluid extraction by hybrid Peng-Robinson equation of state and genetic algorithms
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid model using both genetic algorithms and the Peng-Robinson equation of state is developed for supercritical fluid extraction, where the genetic algorithm is used to generate the non-linear binary interaction parameter of the Peng-Robinson equation of state. Various temperatures, pressures, and solubility found in the literature are used to test the proposed model. The correlation and the mean square errors of the proposed model and the Peng-Robinson equation of state are given in the paper. The predictions of the proposed hybrid model are compared to the conventional model with a Peng-Robinson equation of state in the literature. Generally, the results using the proposed model are better than those using the conventional model because the genetic algorithm used in this paper can provide a better binary interaction parameter to fit the experimental data. The effectiveness of the proposed artificial intelligence approach is demonstrated by simulation and comparison studies.

articleTitle: Periodic steady state solution of coupled PDE-ODE system for CMOS RF circuit simulation
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: We consider the numerical periodic steady state solution of a system of ordinary differential equations and partial differential equations arising from simulation of radio frequency circuits in which the MOSFETs are described by partial differential equations, rather than an equivalent circuit. An efficient iterative algorithm is presented. The algorithm is applied to the simulation of a class C amplifier and results are compared with those obtained by MEDICI.

articleTitle: A system analysis approach for protocol test
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: Systems analysis possesses mature theories and methods. The concepts, models and methods are introduced into the study of the protocol test. The transfer function of the protocol is defined. The system model of the protocol and the protocol stack are presented. The features and abilities of the test methods are analyzed with this approach. The test suite is designed and organized accordingly. All of these concepts give a clearer perception of the protocol and the protocol test, especially the test requirements, which directs and helps the protocol test. This approach is put into practice, and the conformance test of the PPP protocol is presented as an application example.

articleTitle: Using probability network to infer link-level loss rate
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: It is important to obtain link-level performance data, such as loss rate and delay on each segment, which can help us to understand dynamic features of network traffics and identify bottlenecks. This knowledge also assists us to build and construct networks for better performance. Using end-to-end measurement to find link level performance has advantages in eliminating the burden from routers or switches. Instead of using classic statistical methods, such as maximum likelihood estimation, we use the probability network (a direct acyclic graph) to achieve the same goal. In addition, given a loss model, such as Bernoulli, the probability method can dynamically adjust the parameters to trace the traffic change. Simulations based on ns2 were conducted and the data received from the simulations were inferred by a corresponding probability network; the result is very encouraging.

articleTitle: An implementation of sustained real-time radar data recording system on FPGA
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: This paper presents a new architecture for high-speed sustained data recording system, in which real-time and high throughput are two key points. The FPGA implementation of the system controller is given as well. After the I/O bottleneck of conventional storage system structure is analyzed in this paper, a new recording and storage system framework is put forward by aiming to shorten the data transfer path and consequently to reduce the system resource utilization and data transfer latency, contrarily resulting in the improvement of the sustained data recording speed. To satisfy the real-time requirement, a local bus central logic controller module is designed to take the role of former host-side software and to reduce the utilization of host resource and latency caused by the intervention of the host. A speed-matching logic module between the disk in burst transfer mode and the sustained source acquisition data stream is also designed and implemented on a single FPGA chip. The proposed architecture and implementation approaches can be adapted in many applications where real-time and high I/O throughput are required.

articleTitle: A new GIB frequency synchronization algorithm with reduced influence of ISI for OFDM systems
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: The paper analyzes the influence of ISI (intersymbol interference) on the method using the whole guard interval (GI) of the OFDM signal to estimate the fine frequency offset, and then proposes an improved method, which is based on the method of K. Takahashi and T. Saba (see Proc. IEEE GLOBECOM'01, vol.1, p.524-8, 2001). The performances of these methods are simulated under AGWN and 20-ray multipath channel models. The result demonstrate that our proposed method has good performance.

articleTitle: Experimental realization of binary signals transmission using chaos
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: An experimental study of a practical realization to transmit private binary signals using chaos is presented. In particular, we use a generalized Hamiltonian system and observer approach to synchronize two unidirectionally coupled Chua's circuits. Experimental results are in close accordance with the simulations.

articleTitle: Exact minimization of determinant decision diagrams
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: Determinant decision diagram (DDD) is a canonical and compact representation of symbolic expressions in the form of circuit matrix determinants and cofactors for symbolic circuit analysis. DDD-based symbolic analysis algorithms have time and space complexities proportional to the number of DDD vertices. In this paper, we first present a theoretical characterization of the worst-case complexity of the minimal DDDs. We then present an exact algorithm to minimize the number of DDD vertices incorporating both a lower bound and upper bound for pruning the search space. Experimental results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm and the validity of theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: A kind of method of realization of global satellite communication
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: This paper proposes a kind of method to realize global satellite communication, which uses a constellation that covers a specific region, inter-satellite links (ISL), an intelligent network control center (NCC) and intelligent terminals (IT) to constitute a global satellite communication system. It mainly provides a domestic service, and also has the ability to support global communication. Especially, it can provide real-time communication during the whole day throughout the Taiwan Strait and South China Sea without Earth stations abroad. It is also low-cost compared to other global communication systems. As above, this system is meaningful for our country and other countries whose state is similar to China.

articleTitle: Analysis of CDMA RF channel nonlinear distortion
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: Spectral regrowth of a code division multiple access (CDMA) signal passed through a weakly nonlinear circuit are analyzed using power series and statistical method The method yields an analytical expression for the autocorrelation function of the output signal as a the statistical function of the input signal transformed by a behavioral model of the amplifier. It provides helpful predictions of inter-modulation in wireless communication systems with nonlinear distortion effects. This method for the estimation of spectral regrowth for a CDMA signal passed through a nonlinear power circuit have been used in the design of a transceiver for CDMA communication systems.

articleTitle: Small signal analysis of boost converter utilizing V/sup 2/ control technique
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: V/sup 2/ control technique of switching power converter is presented and analyzed in this paper. The small signal model and open-loop small signal transfer function of V/sup 2/ controlled switching power converters have been studied. As the example, the small signal performance analysis of V/sup 2/ controlled boost converter was performed.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of dim moving point target detection algorithms
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: This paper studies the performance comparison of track-before-detect (TBD) and detect-before-track (DBT) multi-frame detection algorithms for the detection of weak moving point targets in infrared image sequences data collected from a scanning sensor. Results indicate that the performance of TBD is superior to that of DBT in all respects for low SNR. However, while computationally simple, DBT can have a reasonable performance only for high SNR. Simulations verify the results of the analysis and the conclusions drawn.

articleTitle: Predicting /spl Sigma//spl Delta/ frequency synthesizer performance
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: This paper describes a nonlinear mathematical model which can be used to predict /spl Sigma//spl Delta/ frequency synthesizer fractional spur and phase noise levels. The model applies to ideal circuits or circuits with nonlinearity, such as mismatch of the phase detector and charge pump. This model was first established based on an ideal circuit and nonlinearity was added next. The model based predictions were compared against circuit-equivalent simulation results and measurement data from a commercial IC. Excellent correlation was achieved. The model also shows that the phase noise is not sensitive to the mismatch while the fractional spur is.

articleTitle: An optimizing clustering algorithm for large-scale mobile network
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: A large-scale mobile communication network, such as military mobile communication system, usually has a two-level topology which is composed of the backbone and the user clustering access network. The difference of the user clustering architecture directly affects the topology of the user access network and the backbone and results in the efficiency of the network. Therefore, it is very important to optimize the user clustering algorithm. This paper suggests a clustering algorithm for a large-scale mobile communication network which can improve significantly the performance of the user access network and optimize the backbone architecture. Simulation results show that this algorithm can achieve the above target.

articleTitle: How to group variables for reducing BDD
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: The reduced order binary decision diagram (ROBDD) is widely used in logic synthesis and verification due to its special characteristics. Most algorithms using ROBDD have polynomial runtimes in the size of the ROBDD. ROBDD varies with different variable orders. So, finding a variable order to make ROBDD small is meaningful in digital circuit design. In this paper, we introduce a novel method to utilize variable relations efficiently. Moreover, for the first time, relations among variable sets are used to reduce BDD further, which is neglected in the past. Experiment results show that our algorithm is effective to reduce ROBDD.

articleTitle: Dynamic end-system resource management for QoS control
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: A novel fine-grained QoS control method, which realizes by dynamic end-system resource management in response to network variation, is presented. Firstly, we presented a model called continuous media action from the global viewpoint. Then the relationships and important conclusions between QoS parameters (rate, delay and jitter) and end system parameters (priority, buffer and buffer management) are analyzed. QoS control strategies based on dynamic resource management in end systems are given. Finally, all of the above are confirmed through a series of tests.

articleTitle: A novel three-phase single-stage zero-switching unity-power-factor power supply
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: A pollution-free high-power switching mode power supply (SMPS) circuit topology is presented, which compounds three-phase PFC with PS-ZVZCS-PWM Inverter Bridge in a single-stage. Its operation process principle and critical parameters are analyzed. Simulation results of a 36 V/400 A prototype show that the PFC of the system is above 0.995 and the zero-switching mode reduces the EMI mostly. Compared with the normal two-stage system, the single-stage power supply has simpler structure, lower cost, higher efficiency and is easier to control.

articleTitle: A new supply approach for a DC-DC control circuit
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: A new supply approach of a DC-DC control circuit is proposed in this paper. Using this new approach, the control circuit energy is provided by the magnetic leakage energy. Operation states of the converter have been analyzed and parameters of components are given.

articleTitle: Calculation of TEAM Problem 21 by the finite volume method
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: The finite volume method (FVM) is presented to investigate the eddy current loss models from TEAM Problem 21. The eddy current distribution at 50 Hz in nonferrous steel plate is calculated. The computed results of the current vector potential T has the same trend as the distribution of the measured result. The magnetic induction B on some certain positions by means of T is also calculated. The comparison of the computed sum of B with the measured B in the same positions shows that the calculated value has the same trend as the measured value and is accurate enough.

articleTitle: Detection of weak periodical signals of fault merged in quasi-random telegram
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: Two problems are presented, one is quasi-random telegram (QT) and the other is cycle-correlation. When signals are so strong that their amplitudes are limited to a certain extent due to the saturation characteristic of devices or testing instruments, then the signals should be changed into QT; there are differences between QT and classic random telegram (RT). Cycle-correlation can be used to detect weak periodic signals merged in noise but classical auto-correlation cannot be used in this case. The difference between cycle-correlation and classical auto-correlation is also given. A computer simulation extracting periodical weak fault signals from the background of QT was carried out. Conclusions for the stationary random process are also provided.

articleTitle: The research of Raman fiber amplifier in 40 Gb/s optical fiber communication system
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: The paper studies the effective core area, nonlinear index, dispersion coefficient, and BER characteristics of two kinds of RFA in a 40 Gbit/s WDM optical communication system. Each system has been optimized on the basis of emulation experiments using PTDS, which is a simulation platform for optical transmission system emulation. A comparison between two kinds of RFA is also made.

articleTitle: The application of satellite positioning technology and its industrialization in China
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: Satellite positioning technology has been widely used in all kinds of military and civil land, marine, space and aeronautical target positioning tasks, navigation activities and accurate surveying measurements since 90s in the last century due to its advantage in providing all weather, real-time, three dimensional and high precision positioning information, as well as speed and accurate timing information. This paper briefly reviews the development of the global satellite positioning and navigation technologies including the basic information of China's "Plough navigation system", introduces the history of satellite positioning technology and its major application fields. The paper also gives an account of the authors' vision for the application and prospect of the satellite positioning technologies in China, and approaches the tactics and stresses of the satellite positioning technology's application and its industrialization future in China.

articleTitle: PCA based programmable path signature analysis in BIST
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: A novel approach of programmable cellular automata (PCA) based switch path signature analysis in built-in self-test (BIST) is presented in this paper. By taking account of the biased output bits of the circuit under test (CUT), while computing the aliasing probability, we can obtain a lower bound of the aliasing probability, contrasting with former methods such as linear feedback shift registers (LFSR) and multiple input shift registers (MISR).

articleTitle: Building semi-immersing human-computer interaction environment of virtual teleconferencing based on multi-screen general projection
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: Building a human-computer interaction environment which supports natural communication and interaction among participant group is the key issue of virtual teleconferencing system, which needs to reestablish the correct space relationship of participants and synthesizing real size video into the virtual environment. We introduce a method that uses multiple projection screens driven by network-connected PCs to construct the spatial and realism semi-immerse virtual teleconferencing environment based on general projection transformation. The experiment shows that participants can interact and collaborate with natural interaction model in there.

articleTitle: Study on frequency synchronization in OFDM systems
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: Frequency synchronization is very important for OFDM systems. Two frequency synchronization algorithms, one in frequency domain and another one in time domain, which are used in different digital television terrestrial broadcasting systems are compared. Computer simulation of these two systems in an equivalent base-band multi-path channel is also given.

articleTitle: Improved energy recovery logic for low power computation
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: In this paper, we analyzed the power consumption in energy recovery circuits; the results show that the non-adiabatic loss is the main cause of power consumption. Based on this fact, an improved energy recovery logic (IERL) structure is proposed. IERL has an additional recovery path and reduces the non-adiabatic loss by improving the recovery percentage through the additional recovery path. From HSPICE simulation result, IERL circuits can greatly improve the low power performance. Complex gate design and cascading of IERL circuits are also considered and are easy to implement. A two-bit full adder of IERL and a sinusoidal power clock generator circuit were fabricated with 0.8 /spl mu/m DPDM CMOS technology and are under test.

articleTitle: An embedded still image code algorithm with rate-distortion optimization
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: An embedded still image coding algorithm with rate-distortion optimization based on human visual weighting is proposed. The rate-distortion optimized embedding code coefficient with decreasing R-D slope, so the first coding bits are ones that have the steepest R-D slope, is used. The distortion can be reduced to the maximum extent per coding bit. The calculation of R-D slope is just a lookup table operation with the help of the probability estimation table of the MQ-adaptive arithmetic coder. The coding speed of the R-D threshold is much faster than the search for the maximum R-D slope. The human visual weighting factor change the order of coding rather than the value of coding. The algorithm has a much faster coding speed and better compression performance.

articleTitle: A new scheme for codebook generation of image VQ
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: Vector quantization (VQ) is an effective means of data compression for it maps a set of real numbers into a single integer. A novel scheme for VQ codebook generation, namely the balance evolution (BE) algorithm, is presented. The proposed scheme decomposes an initial codebook into several sub-sets of closely located codevectors and then designs each sub-codebook using the generalized Lloyd algorithm (GLA) based on a carefully chosen cluster of signal vectors inside the training set. It reduces the variance in contributions of different sub-codebooks to the coding performance by adapting the composition of each training sub-set. Convergence of the proposed procedure is ensured via decreasing the total number of sub-codebooks gradually to one. Experiments show that the BE algorithm outperforms the Linde, Buzo, Gray (1980) algorithm and GLA. However, the achievement is accompanied by an increase in off-line computational complexity.

articleTitle: The quality of service evaluating tool for WAAS
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a software kit for evaluating the Quality of Service (QoS) provided by the Wide Area Augmentation System (WAAS). This tool, named Service Volume Model (SVM), is a professional software providing types of real-time QoS criteria evaluations for WAAS, such as service accuracy, integrity, continuity, availability and safety. Those QoS evaluations can provide the user accurate safety-critical positioning reference information.

articleTitle: Neuromagnetic source parameter estimation of MEG inverse problem by a synthetic nonlinear optimization method
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: The ill-posed MEG (magnetoencephalography) inverse problem draws on a wide range of signal processing techniques. In this paper, we focus on the source localization, i.e., estimating neuromagnetic source parameters by modeling the total source activity in the brain as a single equivalent current dipole. This kind of estimation problem can be solved by nonlinear optimization methods. According to the determination criteria of residual-error-size, the synthetic algorithm proposed here means that we can choose different optimization methods during the source scanning procedure. Computer simulations have been conducted to test the feasibility of the presented approach.

articleTitle: Optimal step-size update equation in nonstationary environment and OVS-LMSII algorithm
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: The least mean square (LMS) algorithm is the most widely used adaptive signal processing algorithm. Many variable step-size LMS algorithms are developed to increase the convergence and lower the steady-state mean-square error (MSE). The optimal variable step-size LMS (OVS-LMS) algorithm exerts its best performance and its convergence rate is nearly the same as the theoretical limit of variable step-size algorithm in the stationary environment. This paper develops the optimal step-size update equation that fits for unknown system changes. Then the robust condition of this equation is analyzed. Finally, the OVS-LMS II, which uses an optimal step-size in the nonstationary environment, is constructed. The computer simulation shows that its rate of convergence and of tracking is nearly the same as the theoretical limit of the variable step-size LMS algorithm.

articleTitle: User detection and PMEPR of MC-CDMA in a multipath fading channel
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: In this paper, a general investigation on the performance of multi-carrier code division multiple access (MC-CDMA) based on the combination of DS-CDMA and multicarrier modulation (also known as OFDM) is provided. Some user-detection methods for the MC-CDMA system are given and several key performance parameters are analyzed. Meanwhile, in this paper, PMEPR in MC-CDMA has been analyzed and the relationship with the aperiodic autocorrelations and the cross-correlations has been established. Based on the relationship, the use of orthogonal Gold codes was proposed over Walsh-Hadamard codes.

articleTitle: MPLS VPN in cellular mobile IPv6 architectures
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: Due to the prevalence of Internet and mobile communications, people sending messages through Internet has concentrated on security and encryption regarding data transmission. The VPN (virtual private network) is the way to keep personal data secure by sending data through the public network. Following the rapid growth of the network and the decrease of IPv4 network addresses, the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) has initiated the promotion of next generation IP (IPv6) instead of the current IPv4. IPv6 supports the mobility and security of mobile communication environments. Since the VPN currently does not support cellular mobile IPv6, the goal of this paper is to construct a MPLS VPN framework in the cellular mobile IPv6 (CMIv6) environment, and use the IPSEC defined by the IETF to keep the security and integrity of data transmission for future mobile communication systems.

articleTitle: Stratospheric telecommunication in 4G
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: Stratospheric telecommunication is expected to be one of the most promising wireless broadband telecommunication strategies in the next decade. It has been designed to have large capacity, broad bandwidth, flexible network forming ability, huge coverage, integrated service ability and definite QoS support. On the other hand, the fourth generation (4G) mobile communication has already been proposed and incurs an ardent discussion with the deployment of the third generation (3G) mobile communication in many countries. The huge bandwidth, ubiquitous computing and seamless multimedia services will almost realize communication which meets the "anytime, anywhere, to anyone, with any way" requirement. We describe the stratospheric telecommunication and its contribution to 4G. The reason and advantages are stated and a specific architecture is given to help further in-depth understanding of the relationship. Some applications are also illustrated.

articleTitle: A simple neural dynamics based tracking controller for a mobile robot
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: In this paper, a simple, yet efficient, neural dynamics based tracking controller for a mobile robot is proposed. The robot velocity in the proposed model is characterized by a biologically inspired shunting equation derived from Hodgkin and Huxley's membrane equation. This model is capable of generating smooth, continuous velocity commands to track arbitrary discrete paths that can be obtained from a real-time path planner. The effectiveness of the proposed controller is demonstrated by simulation studies.

articleTitle: Hierarchical layout design of 8VSB chip
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: 8VSB chip is used to decode the ATSC compliant cable channel signals. This paper presents a new approach to hierarchical layout design of 8VSB chip. Experiments show that our method can accelerate timing convergence and shorten design period.

articleTitle: A method of tumors detection in digital mammography
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: We develop a general method for the detection and segmentation of tumors with an analytical model. It uses a multiresolution wavelet analysis in concert with a Bayesian classifier to identify the possible tumors. The method adaptively chooses thresholds to segment tumors from the background by using a multiscale analysis of the image probability density function. A performance analysis based on a Gaussian distribution model is used to show that the proposed adaptive threshold method is effective in segmenting tumors in mammograms. Examples are presented to demonstrate the efficiency of the technique on a variety of targets.

articleTitle: A 0.35 /spl mu/m CMOS 4.8 Gb/s 4:1 multiplexer
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: A 4.8 Gbit/s 4:1 multiplexer was designed in source coupled logic and fabricated in 0.35 /spl mu/m CMOS technology. It has a power dissipation of less than 1W from a 5V supply and a size of 1/spl times/1.05 mm/sup 2/, and can be directly applied to an optical fiber link at STM-16 (2.488 Gbit/s) level of synchronous digital hierarchy (SDH).

articleTitle: A channel coding architecture adopted in the Digital Television Terrestrial Broadcasting
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: Digital television terrestrial broadcasting (DTTB) has been developing rapidly in recent years. In this paper the channel characters of the DTTB are described. Then a channel coding architecture adopted in the DMB-T (terrestrial digital multimedia/television broadcasting) protocol is presented. This scheme introduces turbo code and turbo-TCM code into DTTB. Simulation results of C/N threshold and bit-error-rate (BER) curves with QPSK and 64QAM modulation have also been shown for this architecture. Compared with other schemes in existing international standards, a conclusion can be drawn that the channel coding scheme presented in this paper has better performance.

articleTitle: Design of software download management for reconfigurable terminals in WCDMA systems
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: This paper introduces key issues of software download management for reconfigurable terminals using common channels in WCDMA systems. Based on the previous work, we introduce in this paper protocols enhancement to the cell-grouping broadcast approach for software download which are mainly used to reduce interference in an interference limited CDMA based system. In addition, it gives the fundamental load based criteria of system level to handover software download traffic between a common channel and a dedicated channel, as is enhanced by the packet indexing based software download strategy. With the introduction of the concept of software download mode, the actions in this mode and protocols of inter-mode handover listed in the this paper gives the realization of software download management in a WCDMA system.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of a parallel-poll virtual output queued switch with two priority levels
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: Development of high performance switches is of paramount importance in high bandwidth connection networks. Input buffered switches with virtual output queues (VOQ) are most impressive because the access rate of crossbar and buffer memory is not higher than the line rate of the connected link. To support various types of traffic with different quality of service (QoS), the packet scheduling algorithms, which solve the contentions in the transfer of data units from an input link to the appropriate output link, must provide different guarantee for different types of traffic. In this paper, based on the parallel-poll VOQ (PP-VOQ) architecture, we propose a simple novel cell scheduling algorithm with two priority levels. We show by simulation that, in the case of cell-based switches, this priority mechanism provide performance advantages over prioritized iSLIP and such an input-queued architecture can provide guaranteed rate, bounded delay, and jitter-restriction for both two priority levels of traffic.

articleTitle: TGSCO: an algorithm for topology generation of clock tree with skew constraint and optimization
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: In this paper, a new clock tree topology generation algorithm TGSCO is proposed for the clock routing. The optimization includes two parts: a constructive stage followed by local topology refinement. During clock tree construction, the skew relationship between clock sinks is considered. Appropriate adjustment to the topology can reduce the delay and skew further. Voronoi diagram is used to accelerate computing. Different from previous methods, our algorithm can produce a clock tree with both balanced topology and short wire length. The experimental results show that the algorithm can control the skew constraints effectively, reduce total wire length, and find an optimized clock tree.

articleTitle: Low-power CMOS VCO and its divide-by-2 dividers with quadrature outputs for 5 GHz/2.5 GHz WLAN transceivers
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: A low power CMOS VCO and its divide-by-2 dividers with quadrature outputs for 5 GHz/2.5 GHz dual band WLAN transceivers are proposed. The VCO is a differential LC oscillator based on an on-chip symmetrical spiral inductor and differential diode. Divide-by-2 dividers with quadrature outputs are implemented by using ILFD (injection-locked frequency divider) techniques. The ILFD structure is similar to that of the VCO to keep its tracking range wide enough. Inductors are optimized by using ASITIC, and differential diodes are designed by careful layout. Due to differential LC tanks and ILFD techniques, power consumption is low. The circuit is implemented in a 0.18 /spl mu/m CMOS process. HSPICE and SpectreRF simulations show that the proposed circuit could produce 5 GHz/2.5 GHz dual band LO signals with a wide tuning range with low phase noise. 2.5 GHz LO signals are quadrature with almost no phase error and no amplitude mismatching. It consumes less than 5.3 mW in the tuning range at VDD=1.5 V. The area is only 1.0/spl times/1.0 mm/sup 2/.

articleTitle: Performance comparison between channel estimation algorithms for TD-SCDMA parallel-interference-cancellation receiver
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: The channel estimation problem for TD-SCDMA parallel interference cancellation (PIC) receiver is considered. Accurate information of channel impulsive response (CIR) is the key to the performance of the receivers. A successive interference-cancellation based estimation method is proposed, and it is compared with the conventional correlation method and the joint channel estimation method by link level simulation with the COSSAP platform. The simulation results show that the suggested channel estimator can provide more accurate estimates than the conventional method under a high-speed vehicular channel.

IEEE Keywords: Time division synchronous code division multiple access

articleTitle: New dormancy policy in novel smart ad hoc sensor system
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: With the development of new technology, the smart ad hoc sensor system which is known as novel wireless mobile sensor networks will be gradually adopted and deployed in many applications. Since there are so many small, lightweight and low-cost wireless sensors in the whole system, the power consumption or dissipation is considered to be a crucial limitation against the successful deployment of these ubiquitous sensor networks. Thus, a policy that saves energy and power is quite necessary. In this paper, we present a new dormancy policy for the novel smart ad hoc sensor system that has dynamic self-adaptive ability. At the same time, simulation has been launched to support our new ideal and schemes.

articleTitle: The research on the electric field sensor with no electrode in x-cut LiNbO/sub 3/
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: This paper reports a new configuration for a Mach-Zehnder interferometer electric field sensor without any electrode utilizing the electro-optic effect in x-cut LiNbO/sub 3/, analyses and discusses the relation between the external electric fields and refractive index change by the use of numerical computation, and presents the process of fabrication. To verify the correctness of the theoretical analysis and feasibility of the sensor, we have conducted direct current experiments for the sensor, and obtained some good results.

articleTitle: 2D AOA estimation of multiple wide-band FM sources based on spatial time-frequency distributions
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: A novel 2D angle-of-arrival (AOA) estimation technique for multiple wide-band FM sources is developed. Based on an L-shaped array, the proposed method employs spatial time-frequency distributions (STFD) in conjunction with a coherent signal-subspace (CSS) processing technique to estimate the direction cosines. CSS processing is achieved by using a unitary constraint interpolation technique over multiple time-frequency points. Computer simulations demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A new family of carrier lock detectors and E/sub s//N/sub 0/ estimators for M-PSK receivers
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: A family of carrier lock detectors for M-PSK receivers operating in AWGN channels is suggested. The statistical properties of the lock detectors are derived theoretically, using stochastic analysis, and computer simulations are used to validate the results obtained. The derivations reveal two useful attributes of the lock detectors: 1) they are self-normalizing (or, in other words, signal-level independent); 2) the channel E/sub s//N/sub 0/ can be readily ascertained from their value when the receiver is in lock. Furthermore, a particularly simple hardware implementation for the lock metric computation process is found, which allows easy and efficient implementation of its computation within an FPGA or ASIC.

articleTitle: Updated extrinsic information for iterative decoding of turbo codes
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: This paper proposes a novel iterative method for turbo codes. This method updates extrinsic information value based on the interim soft outputs to minimize the effects of decoding errors of elementary decoders. The bit error rate performances of turbo codes are simulated, where MAP, log-MAP and MAX-log-MAP based component decoders are employed. Moreover, performances of turbo decoder in the cases that extrinsic information value revised and unrevised are compared in an AWGN channel. It is concluded that the proposed method minimizes the extrinsic information errors, thus the turbo decoder based on the MAX-log-MAP algorithm performs close to that based on MAP and log-MAP algorithms respectively.

articleTitle: Linear mixture model-based image fusion
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: Traditional remote sensing image fusion is based on spectral space. When adding texture information of a high-resolution image to a low-resolution image, the original spectral information of low-resolution image would be distorted more or less. In this paper, a schema to set up a linear relationship between a low-resolution image and a high-resolution image in a different feature space was explored. And then, a look up table based on that relationship was applied to unmix mixture pixels in the low-resolution image respectively. An example was illustrated of unmixing and fusion of the multispectral reflective bands and panchromatic band of a Landsat ETM+ image in Shunyi district, Beijing and obtained a satisfactory fusion result.

articleTitle: Application of nonlinear methods to heart rate variability signal analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: Correlation dimension (D/sub 2/) with spatial embedding and Poincare plots are employed in the nonlinear analysis of heart rate variability among 8 normal subjects, 9 rheumatoid cardiopathy patients, and 6 coronary artery disease patients. Rheumatoid cardiopathy patients and coronary artery disease patients have lower D/sub 2/ compared to the normal subjects. This can serve as a discriminative measure. A proper epoch (N) of the spatial embedding method is 20,000 R-R intervals in this study, upon which the D/sub 2/ value of normal subjects is 5.16. In the analysis of Poincare plots, the normal subjects totally exhibit longer long-axel (L), smaller included angle (/spl alpha/), and relatively regular shape. The bradycardia probability of rheumatoid cardiopathy patients is apparently bigger than the normal's. The coronary artery disease patients show a relatively bigger value of longer long-axel (L). The results and conclusions have been applied in our Holter Analysis System.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional ultrasound imaging diagnostic system under wireless communication networks
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: Three-dimension ultrasound (3DUS) imaging is in routine use in nearly all hospitals and many physician offices and clinics because it offers many benefits compared to other medical imaging techniques. Two of the major benefits are as follows. One is that the equipment of the 2D ultrasound image also is far less expensive to buy and maintain than MRI and CT imaging systems; the other one is that 3DUS imaging has been shown to be valuable for differentiating some aspects of benign and malignant disease. A typical medical image diagnostic system produces data streams which require a very reliable communication, but the environment for transmission, as provided by current and next-generation wireless communication networks, may be lost or within the limits of bandwidth or cause errors. Transmission provisions that avoid catastrophic failure caused by lost or errant packets are therefore very important in order to provide reliable visual communication over such systems. The paper presents an algorithm of 3D medical ultrasound breast tumor diagnostic techniques and resolves the transmission problem over wireless communication networks.

articleTitle: Combined power and rate adaptation in integrated service CDMA communications over Rayleigh fading channels
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: A combined power and rate adaptation in integrated service CDMA communications is considered. The data rate and transmission power is adapted relative to channel variations. For voice services, which require a constant bit rate, we use power adaptation and for data services, rate adaptation is used since data services can tolerate some delay. The analysis results show that this adaptation scheme has a power gain, also a capacity gain, over conventional power adaptation, while maintaining the same average data rates and BER requirements.

articleTitle: A new approach of the adaptive control of nonlinear systems
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: This paper presented H/sup /spl infin// control designs of a complex nonlinear system which can be modeled by a dynamic neural network. Two kinds of new H/sup /spl infin// control design methods are developed. One tries to attenuate both modeling error and the external disturbance to a prescribed level via the H/sup /spl infin// control term, the other tries to attenuate the external disturbance only via the H/sup /spl infin// control, whereas the modeling error is dealt with by a sliding mode control term.

articleTitle: A consistent local congestion avoiding strategy for iterative improvement of cross point assignment
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: Cross point assignment (CPA) is a critical step between global routing and detailed routing. Usually, a CPA algorithm includes two steps:initial CPA and iterative improvement. In this paper, we proposed a consistent local congestion avoiding strategy for CPA iterative improvement based on four congestion lines which describe accurately the local congested area in a congested GRC. The whole strategy consists of three consistent parts: rip up nets crossing congestion lines, re-route (global routing) nets without crossing congestion lines, and avoid crossing congestion line while re-assigning cross points for ripped up nets. By this strategy, we not only avoid local congestion area, but also make fully use of the routing area in congested GRC's. Experimental results show that our strategy can reduce congested GRC's effectively and achieve high completion rate in detailed routing.

articleTitle: An algorithm for blind adaptive multiuser detection based on hidden Markov models
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: The problem of constructing a blind adaptive multiuser detector (MUD) is considered for direct sequence code division multiple access signals transmitted through multipath channels. Due to the slow speed of convergence of channel estimation and existent unreason in state estimation in statistical algorithm based blind adaptive multiuser detection, hidden Markov model theory is proposed as the basis of a new algorithm which uses decorrelation to estimate the multichannel impulse response (MCIR). The algorithm extracts the correlation between the fore states and the back states and increases the speed of channel response estimation. Simulation results illustrate that it has an excellent effect in suppressing multipath interference and resolving the near-far problem, and, at the same time, the algorithm has global convergence and good stability. Under similar condition, the capability of the algorithm is better than that of MABW.

articleTitle: An algorithm to protect TCP bandwidth based on packet-drop history in RED
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: We present an algorithm known as REDBA (RED with Block in Advance) by adding a block gate in front of conventional RED module in a router. REDBA surveys packet-drop history in RED to find non-TCP-friendly flows, and drops the arriving packets from these flows rather than deals with them using RED algorithm. The ability of REDBA algorithm to protect the bandwidth of TCP flows in various circumstances is validated by simulations based on ns2 simulator. Due to its function to punish high-speed flows without end-to-end congestion control mechanism, REDBA is able to provide incentives for promoting this mechanism and be propitious to avoid congestion collapse.

articleTitle: Radar altimeter receiver based on software radio technology
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: A hardware platform and software architecture based on software radio technology is presented and applied to the design of a radar altimeter receiver. According to this structure, we set up a system consisting of two circuit boards; one is a ground echo generator using an FPGA as core chip; the other is a signal processor adopting a combination scheme of DSP and FPGA which has a coherent and an incoherent channel independent of each other to have strong robust capabilities. The flow chart of the software is also given. Experimental results show the method is simple and feasible, it could not only give height and velocity information, but also decrease time to market and thus quickly meet the demands of the end-user.

articleTitle: Capacity performance analysis for multi-service CDMA cellular systems
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: The 3G mobile communication systems based on CDMA are expected to provide multi-services to mobile users. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis on the capacity performance of both uplink and downlink of a multi-service CDMA cellular system. For the uplink, the statistics of the interference at the base station can be approximated by a log normal distributed random variable, and the capacity performance is analyzed through a mathematical approximation method. For the downlink, the distribution of the interference at the mobile user's receiver is hard to gain, thus computer simulation is used to investigate the capacity performance. In addition, the impact of the shadowing, power control error and orthogonality factor on the system capacity performance are evaluated.

articleTitle: Mixed H/sup 2//H/sup /spl infin// estimation: posteriori and priori adaptive filtering
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: We examine the possibility of combining H/sup 2/ (least-mean-squares) performance with H/sup /spl infin//-optimal performance in adaptive filtering. It is shown that the resulting adaptive algorithms allow for a trade-off between average and worst-case performances and are most applicable in situations in which, because of modelling errors, the exact statistics of the underlying signals are not known. A nonlinear adaptive filter that recursively minimizes the LMS error over all filters that guarantees a prespecified worst-case H/sup /spl infin// bound. A simple example is presented to compare the algorithm's behaviour with the H/sup /spl infin// adaptive filter and other mixed algorithms.

articleTitle: A dynamic routing and wavelength assignment algorithm in IP/MPLS over WDM networks
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: The paper investigates the integrated routing (IR) algorithm in IP/MPLS over WDM networks, and presents a simple dynamic IR scheme, bandwidth defragmenting method (BDM). It makes use of the statistical information of link-state and resource availability to determine whether to route an arriving label switched path (LSP) request over the existing topology or to open new wavelength paths. The IR algorithm based on BDM can reduce the number of bandwidth fragments and increase the utility of network resource. Simulation results show that the scheme can improve the performance of the network significantly.

articleTitle: A new algorithm to constructed q-ary cascaded GMW sequences
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: We proposed a new algorithm to construct q-ary cascaded GMW sequences by shift sequences. This algorithm simplified the conventional algorithm that constructed cascaded GMW sequences by the trace function, and it significantly improved the efficiency.

articleTitle: Some dynamical properties for a class of discrete recurrent neural networks
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: This paper studies some dynamical properties of a class of discrete recurrent neural networks. It addresses non-divergence, global attractivity, and complete stability of the networks. Conditions for non-divergence are derived, which not only guarantee non-divergence but also allow for the existence of multi-equilibrium points. Under these nondivergence conditions, global attracting compact sets are obtained. Complete stability is studied via a novel energy function and the Cauchy Convergence Principle. Examples and simulation results are used to illustrate the theory.

articleTitle: A new approach to estimate noise distribution under chaotic background
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of filtering noise out from a chaotic signal. To pursue this aim, we prefer to estimate noise distribution under chaotic background first. Since chaotic signal has internal random property, it's hard to filter the noise out with a normal method. On the basis of the extensive analysis of the local correlation of the chaotic dynamic system, a method for analyzing a signal's deterministic degree is given. A parameter D being very sensitive to the noise is introduced and used to show how deterministic the system is. A new approach for estimation of noise distribution in chaotic distribution system is obtained.

articleTitle: SDH link rate calculation for connecting multiple Ethernets
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: As the throughput of Ethernet migrates from 10/100 Mbps to Gigabits, users' desire to expand Ethernet scope grows simultaneously. However, the CSMA/CD mechanism restricts the maximum scope of Ethernet. Therefore, utilizing SDH/SONET, a technology for transmitting data over long distance, to overcome such limit has become promising. Different from the common solutions, which only support point-to-point connection of two Ethernets, the solution proposed here is applicable to more complex network topology. In addition, a model for the traffic generated by multiplexed hosts is put forward and the transmission rate on the SDH link to provide the prescribed QoS is calculated.

articleTitle: The application of unequal power assignment strategy in AMR
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: An unequal power assignment strategy for the up-link of a 3G system is proposed in this paper, which aims to maximize the admission capacity of wireless communication systems. Through the analysis of multiple access interference (MAI) for the up-link, the formula to calculate the optimal power ratio for multimedia traffic is deduced. The performance of the novel strategy on the 3GPP-FDD system with integrated speech and data traffic has been investigated and compared with the traditional equal power assignment (EPA) strategy. Simulation results reveal that unequal power assignment outperforms EPA. The application of the unequal power assignment strategy in an adaptive multi-rate (AMR) system is investigated. Simulation results show that different AMR modes have a different influence on admission capacity in 3G systems.

articleTitle: Blind separation of jointly stationary correlated sources
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: The separation of unobserved sources from mixed observed data is a fundamental signal processing problem. Most proposed techniques for solving this problem rely on the independence of, or at least the assumption of uncorrelation of, the source signals. The paper introduces a technique for cases that the source signals are correlated with each other. The method uses the Wold decomposition principle for extracting the desired and proper information from the predictable part of the observed data, and exploits approaches based on second-order statistics to estimate the mixing matrix and source signals. Simulation results are provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: A new approach to adaptive blind MMSE multiuser detection
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: A new adaptive blind multiuser detector is proposed. The algorithm is founded on minimizing the mean squared error (MSE) but does not require training sequences, and converges to the minimum MSE (MMSE) detector. Like the blind minimum-output-energy (MOE) detector, the proposed detector requires only the signature waveform and timing of the user of interest. We show that the blind MMSE and MOE detectors have similar transient and steady-state performance, and the same level of robustness against imprecise estimation of the desired user's received signature waveform. However, the proposed adaptive detector has 2N+1 fewer multiplications and N fewer summations than the MOE detector, where N is the length of the tap-weight vector.

articleTitle: Accurate resource reservation over SRP ring
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: When performing RSVP based resource reservations over SRP ring, the layer 2 queuing and forwarding considerably increases the burstiness of data streams, and makes it hard to allocate resources and guarantee QoS. In this paper, the burstiness variation bounds for high priority data streams over the SRP ring was estimated through theoretical analysis. Using the results of this paper, we could make more accurate resource reservations over the SRP ring and effectively guarantee flow QoS.

articleTitle: A 8-bit MCU design using a four-pipeline architecture
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: It is found that through improving the system architecture of PIC16C57's, the microcontroller's (MCU) execution efficiency can be improved apparently. Two-pipeline architecture in PIC16C57 is replaced by a four-pipeline architecture. Experiment results verify that the designed MCU is compatible functionally with PIC16C57, its execution efficiency is 4 times as high as that of PIC16C57, its system clock reaches above 60MHz.

articleTitle: Smart antenna technology for the reverse link of WCDMA systems
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: An efficiently combined structure of a smart antenna array and a conventional RAKE combiner is presented and applied to the pilot symbol-assisted reverse link in a WCDMA system. According to the frame structure of WCDMA, we use a least-mean-square (LMS) adaptive array processing algorithm, which uses the spreading sequences of pilot symbols of each slot as the reference signals for updating the weight vectors of the antenna arrays. The simulation results show the method is simple and practical, and improves the capacity of the system greatly, thus solving the capacity problem of the reverse channel of WCDMA systems.

articleTitle: Hopf bifurcation analysis on a two-neuron system in the frequency domain
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: In this paper, we study a two-neuron system with distributed delays in the frequency domain. Allowing the mean delay as a-bifurcating parameter and using the Nyquist criterion, we obtain that Hopf bifurcation occurs for a weak kernel, and analyze the direction and stability of the bifurcating periodic solutions.

articleTitle: Design and application of SDH pointer leakage ASIC MXTULPx8-5
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: The development of the synchronous digital hierarchy (SDH) technique relies on the evolution of ASICs. This paper introduces the characteristics of the SDH pointer leakage ASIC MXTULPx8-5, which has been designed independently by the E&E Department of Tsinghua University. This chip can compensate for plesiochronous relationships between incoming and outgoing higher level (AU4) synchronous payload envelope frame rates through processing of the lower level (TU11, TU12, or TU3) tributary pointers, so that the aligned tributaries can be easily column switched by the SDH tributary unit cross-connect chip. The time-sliced multiplexing design method is introduced as the key technique, and the tributary elastic buffer size is calculated. The application example of MXTULPx8-5 is also described.

articleTitle: Diversity transform for decision-feedback differential detection of N-DPSK for a correlated Rayleigh fading channel
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: We investigate a diversity scheme which employs a simple transform, symbol interleaving and decision-feedback differential detection (DF-DD) for differential phase-shift-keying signal transmission over a correlated Rayleigh fading channel. The proposed scheme merits instinct time diversity within each transmitted block and thus presents patent resistance to fading. It is shown that the proposed diversity scheme employing DF-DD significantly outperforms the previously reported diversity scheme employing two-symbol differential detection.

articleTitle: A research on self-organizing software radio network
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: In this article we carry out research on the self-organizing software radio network. First, we introduce the key technologies, including the network control and management architecture, the routing protocols, the network-resource management and dynamic traffic equalization, and the technology of software radio serving as a gateway. Secondly, we describe the unique set of challenging problems while designing the self-organizing software radio network, which differ from traditional wireless systems and wired networks. Finally, we present an approach to the further study of the self-organizing network.

articleTitle: Implement a network intrusion detection system using a design pattern: virtual interface machine to improve decoupling and efficiency of development?
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: In this paper, we present a design pattern called Virtual Interface Machine to tackle relative problems in software design and describe its application in our network intrusion detection system. We point out the main drawbacks of the present design pattern about decoupling and efficiency of development. Virtual Interface Machine could let us easily separate UI from logic layer, decouple components of UI entirely and enjoy efficiency of RAD in UI design without compromising reusability and maintainability of the whole design. By thorough decoupling, we could even change both the logic layer and UI at run time, which is impossible on other patterns.

articleTitle: An error robust macro-block mode decision for H.26L stream
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: With the rapid development of the Internet, more and more attention is focused on IP video streaming. We introduce an RD optimal macro-block mode decision scheme for the new H.26L video stream. Based on the statistical error propagation model of the Internet and the unequal NAL packet of H.26L, our new scheme can be more error robust than those currently adopted in the H.26L test mode.

articleTitle: A cellular wireless location for W-CDMA
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: The location service in cellular systems has become very important in recent years. This paper discusses the wireless location method which is based on the time difference of arrival (TDOA) in the wideband code division multiple access and proposes a new method by adding some beacons in the cell. It prevents the necessity of more than three bases participating in the location for the conventional method, and reduces the cochannel interference. In addition, this paper presents the results of the simulation and analysis of performance too.

articleTitle: Adaptive modulation and power allocation for multicarrier DS/CDMA
publicationTitle: IEEE 2002 International Conference on Communications, Circuits and Systems and West Sino Expositions
abstract: To satisfy the request for high data rate and high frequency efficiency for new generation communication systems, an adaptive modulation method, subcarrier and power allocation is proposed for multicarrier DS/CDMA systems. With the downlink channel parameter acquired from the uplink channel feedback, an optimization algorithm is utilized to maximize frequency efficiency and minimize the required transmitting power for a given QoS and data throughput.
